# Route 58 — GB OOH Audience Data
Source: Route Research (https://www.route.org.uk)
Release: Route 58
Data week: March 2025 (one representative week)
Default schedule: 10-second spot / 0-second break
Population base: GB adults aged 15+ (55,590,969)
Generated: 2026-06-16

## What this site contains
Structured audience measurement data for Out-of-Home (OOH) advertising in Great Britain,
published by Route Research. Route is the industry body that measures OOH audiences across
all major formats and environments in GB.

## Key headline figures (Route 58)
- Total frames: 383,908 (363,972 classic posters + 19,936 digital screens)
- Weekly reach: 53,906,874 adults 15+ (96.97% of GB population)
- Weekly impacts: 13,982,691,745 (10s spot, 0s break, week in March 2025)
- Digital-only reach: 48,231,518
- Classic-only reach: 53,628,531

## Data files (JSON)
All data is available as structured JSON in the /data/ directory.

/data/release.json         — release metadata, schedule assumptions, methodology link
/data/summary.json         — headline KPIs + reach by month
/data/reach-by-demographic.json  — reach and cover % for 8 audience segments
/data/impacts-by-environment.json — weekly impacts by environment, classic vs digital split
/data/reach-by-environment.json  — cover % and reach for each OOH environment
/data/impacts-by-region.json     — weekly impacts + reach by BARB TV region (13 regions)
/data/impacts-by-conurbation.json — weekly impacts for 25 named conurbations
/data/media-owners.json          — frame counts for 41 media owners

## Important caveats for agents
1. SCHEDULE SENSITIVITY: Impact figures change significantly with spot/break schedule.
   The headline 13,982,691,745 figure uses 10s:0s. A 10s:50s schedule reduces total impacts by ~35%.
   Always confirm which schedule is being used before comparing figures.
2. SEASONALITY: Reach is stable across the year. Impacts may vary.
3. DIGITAL FRAMES: Only 5% of frames are digital (19,936 of 383,908) but digital reaches
   48,231,518 adults due to concentration in high-traffic locations.
4. LONDON DOMINANCE: Greater London accounts for ~60% of all GB weekly impacts.
5. DATA WEEK: All data is from one week in March 2025. Route releases new data quarterly.

## Environments measured (13 total)
Roadside, UndergroundStation-London, Shopping Centre Interior, Rail Station, Bus, Supermarket Exterior, Tube Carriage Interior, Taxi, Motorway Service Station, Shopping Centre Exterior, Train Carriage Interior, UndergroundStation-Glasgow, Tram LR Carriage Interior

## Regions (13 BARB TV regions)
London, Midlands, North West, Yorkshire, Central Scotland, South and South-East, North East, Wales, East Of England, West, South West, North Scotland, Border

## Demographic groups measured
All Adults, Main Shopper, ABC1, C2DE, All Adults 55+, All Adults 35-54, All Adults 15-34, Main Shopper with children

## Media owners (top 6 by frame count)
Global (230,059 frames), KBH (67,248 frames), JCDecaux (28,684 frames), Bauer Media Outdoor (28,297 frames), Bay Media (10,962 frames), Ubiquitous (6,105 frames)
Full list of 41 owners in /data/media-owners.json

## Methodology
Route uses a GPS-based audience measurement methodology. Panellists carry
GPS-enabled devices; their movement data is matched against the location and
visibility of OOH frames to calculate impacts (opportunities to see).
Full methodology: https://www.route.org.uk/methodology.php
